chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Mansur ibn Hazim from Bakr ibn Habib, who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'What should I say in the Tashahhud and the Qunut?' He said, 'Say with the best of what you know, for if it were fixed/limited, the people would be lost.'

key_terms.التَّشَهُّد: Tashahhud, the testimony of faith and praise recited in prayer
key_terms.اَلْقُنُوت: Qunut, a supplication recited in prayer, often before or after bowing
key_terms.لَهَلَكَ اَلنَّاسُ: The people would be lost/perished (due to hardship)

ai.seo_question: What should I recite in Tashahhud and Qunut if there is no fixed text?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the principle of *ease* (yusr) in worship, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that the core essence of supplication outweighs rigid textual uniformity. By stating that a fixed text would cause the 'loss of the people' (halaaka al-nas), the Imam highlights the practical necessity of accommodating varying levels of literacy and memorization among the general populace. This flexibility ensures that the spiritual connection in prayer remains accessible to all, preventing undue hardship (haraj) in fulfilling this pillar of Islam.
